state.seed_assertion: DPO advice on whether processing is compliant and can go ahead should be sought and documented as part of sign-off; if advice is not followed, reasons must be recorded.

sentences.1: DPO advice on whether processing is compliant and can go ahead should be sought and documented as part of sign-off;
sentences.2: if advice is not followed, reasons must be recorded.
sentences.3: As part of the sign-off process, you should seek and document DPO advice on whether the processing is compliant and can go ahead.
sentences.4: If you decide not to follow their advice, you need to record your reasons.
sentences.5: If a DPO is present in the organization, the controller must seek the DPO's advice on the DPIA and document it as part of the process.
sentences.6: If you have a Data Protection Officer (DPO), you must ask for their advice on your DPIA, and document it as part of the process.
sentences.7: Views of individuals or their representatives should be sought and documented unless there is a good reason not to.
sentences.8: If a DPIA is determined not to be needed, the decision and reasons must be documented, including the DPO's advice.
sentences.9: The advice and recommendations of the DPO should be recorded in a DPIA where relevant and the DPIA should be signed off by appropriate people.
sentences.10: A DPIA submission to the ICO must include descriptions of roles and responsibilities of joint controllers or processors, processing purposes and methods, protective measures and safeguards, DPO contact details, and a copy of the DPIA itself.
sentences.11: contact details of your DPO (if you have one);
sentences.12: A schedule for regularly reviewing the DPIA or reviewing it when processing changes should be agreed and documented.
